svg.title: Four kinds of verification, in order of strength
svg.desc: Most verification questions are decided deterministically by string resolution, set membership, schema invariants and dataflow tests. A bounded prover discharges proof obligations such as pairwise disjointness for UNIQUE decision tables, returning proved only when the enumeration was exhaustive and unknown otherwise. A model is used only where judgment is irreducible, and it never sees the prior answer. Human expertise is reserved for legal correctness.
svg.text: Most verification is not a matter of opinion.
Push every question down to the strongest check that can settle it — and judge only what is left.

g.text: Decided by code, reproducible by anyone
Does the quote occur in the cited chunk? · Does this rule id exist? · Does the schema hold? · Does B read what A assigns?
2 · PROOF · BOUNDED, SOUND, INCOMPLETE BY DESIGN
Proved exhaustively — or returned as unknown
Does this UNIQUE table satisfy pairwise disjointness? · Can this condition be satisfied at all?
3 · MODEL · ONLY WHERE JUDGMENT IS IRREDUCIBLE
Judged — against fresh evidence, never the prior answer
Does this description faithfully state the obligation? · Evidence is rebuilt from the raw corpus, so errors do not correlate.
Is this a correct reading of the regulation?
The one question no check above can answer — which is why it should not be spent on the ones they can.

svg.text: The difference is not a better judge. It is far fewer questions that need judging — and a proof where a proof is possible.
